span: the delay should have been condoned within the four corners of the statute
why: Court holds the tribunal erred in refusing to condone a 5-day delay because the explanation was sufficient.

span: we are inclined to allow the appeals, set aside the impugned order, condone the delay in filing appeal before the High Court
why: Court itself condones the delay in filing the appeal on reasons of illness.

span: it is not mandatory to file an application in writing before relief can be granted under the said section
why: Court reasons that s.5 Limitation Act empowers condonation and does not require a written application; the next paragraph states this as the law that emerges.

span: Delay is condoned – Matter remanded to High Court to be decided on merit
why: Headnote holding: s.173 MV Act gives discretion to condone delay on sufficient cause, liberally construed; 45-day delay condoned.

span: Delay rightly not condoned by the High Court
why: Holding: a 1942-day delay was not sufficiently explained, so condonation was rightly refused.

span: Delay of 554 days in filing the appeal before High Court is condoned, subject to costs of Rs.10,000/-
why: Holding: illness was sufficient cause and the Supreme Court itself condones the delay.

span: Hence, High Court was right in dismissing s.5 application of the appellant
why: Holding: delay of 254 days not explained by lack of funds, so refusal to condone is upheld.
